title: RedTide maritime edge onramp ramblings
content:
Call notes 2026-02-26 - kickoff with RedTide ops + infra (CTO Samir Khan, infra lead Nora Hale)

Quick context (1 line): RedTide runs a small fleet ops stack on vessels with spotty connectivity; want local inference for document summarization (manifests/paperwork) + triaging incident reports, with fallback to hosted Redwood when connectivity available.

Attendees: Samir (RedTide CTO), Nora (infra), Jess (fleet ops), Aisha (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood solutions)

Primary asks / outcomes they want:
- Autonomous summarization pipeline for arrival/departure manifests (reduce human read-time)
- Fast classification (safety/incident triage) at <300ms p95 on edge box for binary classification tasks
- Embeddings for onboard search of past incidents (on-prem index)
- Offline-first behavior: process locally and sync summaries when bandwidth permits
- Compliance: customer cannot send raw manifests off-ship (sensitive contracts).

Key constraints / gotchas surfaced:
- Hardware on vessel edge nodes: 1x A10G or equivalent, occasional thermal throttling during heavy compute windows (midday).
- Persistent storage is small (200GB available per vessel) — embeddings index must be compact and pruning-friendly.
- Network: multi-hour blackouts predictable in coastal runs; when online they use a leased-satellite link with asymmetric bandwidth (upload limited).
- Data retention: legal requires 30 days of onboard logs; long-term archive must go to their central S3 when connected.
- Security: strict key handling; they prefer HSM/KMS integration within customer VPC and want audit logs for every model invocation.
- Sequence lengths: manifests are long (5–12k tokens typical) — summarization must support long-context or preprocessing chunking.

Initial technical sketch / SE thoughts:
- Model split: tiny BERT-style classifier quantized (INT8/4-bit) for triage -> meets 300ms p95 on A10G with single-thread inference. Use Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching = 1 / low coalescing to hit latency SLO.
- Summarization: use a mid-sized long-context model (e.g., Llama2-13B-8k or a longformer variant). If memory constrained, offload KV cache to disk/SSD and apply chunk+stitch summarization pipeline. Consider Redwood runtime kernel selection to balance perf.
- Embeddings: use compact 1k-d float16 or PQ-compressed vectors; maintain local Faiss index with periodic pruning TTL to fit 200GB cap. Optionally embed only incident metadata (not full text) to reduce size.
- Fallback policy: when VPC external connectivity present, route heavy summary jobs to Hosted Redwood Dedicated pool with encrypted transit; local inference remains default.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated manifest patterns; also keep a tiny LRU for recent ship IDs to avoid re-tokenizing common headers.

Performance/ops considerations:
- Batching: for classification keep batch size 1; set max batching window 10ms. For summarization allow batching up to 4 if background/async.
- Memory: watch peak KV cache behaviour on long sequences; add guard rails to drop prefixes > 8k and fallback to chunking.
- Telemetry: surface token-level latency breakdown to ops console + per-route error counts. They asked for per-vessel dashboard tile.
- Cost: rough monthly estimate per vessel (compute + storage + license) = $1.2k–$2.5k depending on model choice and sync frequency — present as range.

Prototype plan (0 → PoC in 6 weeks):
Week 0 (this week): narrow scope: proof-of-concept on one vessel image + sample manifest dataset. Get NDA + sample data.
Week 1–2: build minimal local runtime image (Redwood Private base) with classifier + minimal summarizer pipeline (chunk+merge). Add simple Faiss index.
Week 3: deploy to test vessel (or lab box with simulated network blackouts). Measure p95/classification latency, summarization throughput, disk use.
Week 4: iterate on quantization + batching, integrate KMS for key wrap proof-of-concept.
Week 5: sync workflow with Hosted fallback test (simulate degraded local compute + network).
Week 6: demo, final notes, ops runbook draft and next contract discussion.

Open questions to clarify with them:
- Can they provide 3 representative manifests (large, medium, small) with redaction if needed? (asked Samir)
- Are there regulatory tags that necessitate zero-retention for specific fields? (Jess to confirm)
- Do they have an existing HSM vendor for KMS integration (YubiHSM / AWS CloudHSM)? Nora to check.
- Vessel onboard OS image preferences e.g., Ubuntu 20.04 vs 22.04? Also container runtime (containerd vs docker).

Immediate action items (owners):
- Aisha: produce a short PoC checklist + estimated infra footprint (by 2026-03-04).
- Liam: prepare quantization options matrix (INT8 vs 4-bit) and sample perf numbers on A10G (by 2026-03-06).
- Nora (RedTide): provide sample manifests and confirm HSM vendor (by 2026-03-05).
- Marco: set up Confluence PoC page and link to RD Jira (done: see linked_artifacts).

Misc notes / UX desires from Jess + product team:
- Want canned prompt templates for manifest summarization: top-line (3 bullets), cargo anomalies, next actions.
- Prefer an "operator mode" with one-button reprocess for last 24h of manifests.
- Dark-mode logging UI (joke, but ops actually likes fewer whites).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: thermal throttling causing latency spikes during midday -> mitigation: schedule heavy batch summarization in night window + add throttling-aware autoscaling policy on dedicated pool fallback.
- Risk: index growth -> mitigation: implement TTL-based pruning and compact PQ compression.
- Risk: data leak during sync -> mitigation: enforce envelope encryption + signed upload and audit logs.

Notes for demo script:
- Start with a long manifest, run local summarizer, show p95 latency and token breakdown, then simulate offline->online sync to hosted fallback, show audit trail.
- Highlight cost delta when using quantized classifier vs unquantized.

End of notes — keep informal. This doc to evolve into PoC runbook once we have sample data.
